author: Mark Atwood
text:
Escalating: this is a workspace-canonical-template decision with public-API breaking scope across all 7 extension-client crates.

Status check (2026-05-17):
* mail-client (the canonical extension-client template per workspace AGENTS.md): only `pub mod methods;` at the root + `pub use methods::{...}`. No `pub mod session/sse/types/utils/ws` because those modules don't exist there.
* chat-client diverges with 6 `pub mod` declarations because it has SSE/WS/push that no other client has.
* All 7 client crates have `pub mod methods;` at the root — that IS the canonical pattern.

Decision split:

A. **`pub mod methods` across all 7 crates** — workspace-canonical pattern. Changing chat-client to `pub(crate)` here would break the cookie-cutter rule. Per the bead's own framing ("A workspace-wide decision is needed before this can be acted on"), the right resolution is a workspace propagation epic, not a chat-client-scoped change. That epic would need to file a `JMAP-*-pubmod` bead with 7 children, one per client crate.

B. **Chat-client-specific `pub mod session/sse/ws`** — these contain items already re-exported at the crate root via `pub use session::{...}` / `pub use sse::{...}` / `pub use ws::{...}`. Tightening to `pub(crate) mod session/sse/ws` would collapse the dual paths to one. This is chat-client-only and could land independently of (A) — but it WOULD set precedent for whether future siblings adding SSE/WS keep their modules `pub` or `pub(crate)`.

C. **`pub mod types/utils`** — items are NOT re-exported at the root, so `pub mod` is the only path. Tightening here would make these items unreachable. Either keep `pub mod` AND re-export at the root (matches the convention used for every other module), or commit to the inner path as canonical and document it.

Recommendation if forced to choose:
* (A) — file a workspace propagation epic JMAP-*-pubmod, do NOT touch chat-client unilaterally.
* (B) — defer until (A) is decided; (B)'s precedent-setting implications make it best resolved by the same epic.
* (C) — easiest to ratify here: pick "re-export at root + keep pub mod" to match the existing convention. Doc the dual paths.

Options for the human:
1. Approve (B)+(C) chat-client-scoped now, file (A) as workspace epic for later. Smallest, most reversible change.
2. Defer all three to a workspace epic. Cleanest, but parks the bead until that epic runs.
3. Decide otherwise — e.g. keep `pub mod` everywhere as a deliberate "both paths are committed" stance and pick option 2 from the bead description (document both paths as committed). This is the most conservative and breaks nothing.

Filing this for human judgment because the decision is public-API breaking across 7 crates (workspace AGENTS.md "When NOT to file human" anti-pattern 3 explicit exception).
